new_findings.problem: The new wrapper detects changed authority only after original_admit has already used its unverified target fields. With port replaced by 8756, adapter.py:1086,1092 allows the value and calls p4.listener_owner(8756), which runs Get-NetTCPConnection on that port (P4 controller.py:248-250). Replacing only parent_identity.pid while retaining run/origin also causes p4.identity(unissued_pid) at adapter.py:1081-1082,358-363 before any wrapper rejection. No off-scope launch is needed for these off-scope native reads. The existing replacement test records only simulated launches in its assertion at test_root_inert_invocation.py:528-535, despite its mock recording listener query targets at line 103.
new_findings.required_fix: Bind the actual input consumed by original admission to the issued bytes before any target-directed lookup, while retaining the effective-state checks after original admission. A separate path prehash leaves a reopen gap. Have ROOT rule on a narrowly scoped private read binding if needed. In pure tests record every native PID/port lookup and assert that substituted targets are never observed.

new_findings.problem: The successful close belongs to the file created at line 388. The hardlink at line 389 resolves its source by pathname again. Replacing the closed pending path with a different ordinary file during that interval makes os.link publish the replacement successfully. no_reparse permits ordinary files. The caller still returns its in-memory record and may exit 0, although the canonical bytes can differ from the witness it durably closed. The close-failure and destination-collision tests do not substitute the source. ROOT independent readback can catch the mismatch; the publisher itself does not.
new_findings.required_fix: Bind publication success to the originally serialized result bytes and closed object. At minimum compare canonical bytes against the exact expected bytes before returning an eligible process outcome, require identical ROOT readback and preserve failure evidence without overwrite. If canonical presence itself must certify closed-source identity, use an identity-bound publication mechanism or a ROOT-owned enforced exclusion across close/link. Cover a regular-file source substitution after close in a mock.
